quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks can you have before driving is affected?

options.text: Three
Two
One

questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Do not drive after drinking any amount of alcohol. Even one drink will affect your driving ability.

questions.question: What is the best way to practice defensive driving?

options.text: Scan the road ahead.
Rubberneck.
Stare straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Scan the road ahead.
questions.explanation: Stay alert and scan the road ahead. This helps you see hazards early and gives you time to react safely.

questions.question: What does a red octagon-shaped sign say?

options.text: Do not enter.
One-way.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop at this sign.

questions.question: What should you do when you reach a broken traffic signal?

options.text: Stop completely, then yield the right-of-way before entering.
If the intersection is clear, you don't need to stop.
Drive quickly through to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then yield the right-of-way before entering.
questions.explanation: When a traffic signal is not working, treat it as an all-way stop. Come to a complete stop and look before entering the intersection, unless a police officer is directing traffic.

questions.question: Which factor affects how fast your body absorbs alcohol?

options.text: Weight
Height
Intelligence

questions.correctAnswerText: Weight
questions.explanation: Weight, biological sex, food in your stomach, and the amount of alcohol consumed all affect how fast your body absorbs alcohol. Only time can remove alcohol from your system.

questions.question: When driving on a one-way street, when can you turn left onto another one-way street?

options.text: If you speed up before the turn.
If traffic moves to the right.
If traffic moves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: If traffic moves to the left.
questions.explanation: You can turn left onto a one-way street only if traffic on that street moves to the left. You cannot turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves to the right.

questions.question: What should you do if a car is tailgating you on a multilane highway?

options.text: Speed up to match the car behind you.
Move right and let the other car pass.
Slow down to bother the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move right and let the other car pass.
questions.explanation: If you're in the left lane and being tailgated, move to the right lane to let the car pass. The left lane is for faster traffic to pass slower traffic.

questions.question: What color and shape are construction zone signs?

options.text: Square or rectangular with white and red.
Round or octagonal with black and yellow.
Diamond or rectangular with orange and black.

questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond or rectangular with orange and black.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs have orange backgrounds with black letters or symbols. They appear on the right side of the road, or on both sides on divided highways.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Steep grade ahead.
The road ahead has turns or curves.
Slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that the pavement becomes slippery when wet and is harder to drive on safely.

questions.question: What is a dangerous habit in work zones?

options.text: Following another vehicle too closely.
Not watching for workers and equipment.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: In work zones, slow down and keep distance from other vehicles. Watch carefully for workers and equipment on the road.

questions.question: What should a driver do about right-of-way rules?

options.text: Assume all drivers follow the rules.
Assume most drivers follow the rules.
Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Do not assume you have the right-of-way. Always look at the situation and be prepared to yield if it helps prevent a crash.

questions.question: How do stopping distance and crash severity relate to speed?

options.text: They decrease as speed increases.
They are not affected by speed.
They increase as speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: They increase as speed increases.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds mean longer stopping distances and more severe crashes.

questions.question: What does this speed limit sign mean?

options.text: You must drive at exactly 55 mph through the intersection.
The maximum speed is 55 mph under ideal conditions.
You must not drive slower than 55 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum speed is 55 mph under ideal conditions.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs tell you the maximum speed for that road. You may drive slower based on road conditions, but you cannot drive faster than the posted limit.

questions.question: If you see a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane:

options.text: The pedestrian must yield the right-of-way.
You must yield the right-of-way.
Honk your horn to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog means the pedestrian is blind or partially blind. You must always give them the right-of-way.

questions.question: Strong wind gusts on highways:

options.text: Generally affect only large vehicles.
Only cause visibility problems.
Can cause problems for all vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause problems for all vehicles.
questions.explanation: Strong wind affects all drivers. It can reduce visibility by blowing dust onto the road and can physically push any vehicle off course.

questions.question: Any amount of alcohol in your blood may affect your:

options.text: Right-of-way privileges.
Judgment and physical coordination.
Knowledge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment and physical coordination.
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol can impair your judgment and coordination. This can happen even below the legal limit. Driving under the influence can result in criminal charges.

questions.question: Highway driving requires you to:

options.text: Be able to safely drive at higher speeds.
Stay alert at all times.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Safe highway driving requires constant alertness and the ability to drive at high speeds.

questions.question: If you text while driving, you are ____ times more likely to crash than a non-distracted driver.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving increases your crash risk 20 times. Reading or writing a text takes your eyes off the road for about 4.6 seconds. At 55 mph, this is like driving the length of a football field blindfolded.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: You can eliminate them with one outside mirror on each side.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.
You can see blind spots in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Large trucks have much larger blind spots than passenger vehicles, and other drivers should avoid these areas.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: You can eliminate them with one outside mirror.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.
You can check blind spots by looking in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Even with proper mirrors, all vehicles have blind spots you cannot see. Large trucks have much larger blind spots than passenger vehicles.

questions.question: If you are driving on a highway next to a single broken white line:

options.text: You cannot cross the line to pass.
You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
You may only cross the line to change lanes if you are in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
questions.explanation: White dashed lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross a dashed white line to pass or change lanes if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When can you legally drive around or under a railroad crossing gate?

options.text: Never.
When you can see clearly in both directions.
When the warning lights are not flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never go around or under a lowered railroad crossing gate. After the gate is raised, only cross the tracks when you can see clearly in both directions and are sure no trains are coming.

questions.question: Excessive speed:

options.text: Does not increase crash risk.
Improves your ability to react to hazards.
Often leads to dangerous decisions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often leads to dangerous decisions.
questions.explanation: Excessive speed is a major cause of crashes. It does not save time and often leads to dangerous driving decisions.

questions.question: To enter a gap in highway traffic:

options.text: Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
Speed up and let other vehicles make way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes or entering traffic, make sure no vehicles are in your way. Always check for traffic on the side and behind your vehicle before moving.

questions.question: You are in a left-turn lane at an intersection with oncoming traffic. You should:

options.text: Move to the left of the center lane.
Signal before you arrive at the intersection.
Turn your front wheels to the left to prepare to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal before you arrive at the intersection.
questions.explanation: Begin signaling about 100 feet before you turn left. Keep your front wheels straight until it is safe to turn. This prevents another vehicle from pushing you into oncoming traffic if it hits you from behind.
